paper.title: A Theory of Time-Sensitive Language Generation: Sparse Hallucination Beats Mode Collapse
paper.summary: Introduces deadline-sensitive lower and upper density, proves impossibility barriers for consistent or linear-time generation, gives a randomized nearly-linear-time half-density algorithm with vanishing hallucination, and separates timely upper from lower density.

formalization_scope.summary: The deterministic finite-prefix, density-transfer, deadline-diagonal, feasible-profile, measure-zero-chain, and greedy-counting cores are formalized. For Theorem 4, a documented queue-totalized GCG proves stage progress, eventual consistency, cofinal checkpoints, and the universal half-density lower guarantee; a concrete online adaptive exact presentation with logarithmically sparse catch-up proves the matching upper endpoint and unconditional worst-case instance-level equality. The randomized and almost-sure layers of Theorems 1--3 remain open.
specializations: Timely lower and upper densities are currently instance-level quantities; the paper's outer infima over targets, enumerations, and collections are not separately packaged.
Deadline and feasible-profile constructions use natural-valued zero-based prefixes and explicit unboundedness witnesses.
The repaired Theorem 4 endpoint queues every Accurate guess rather than only strict-superset transitions, closing the source algorithm's early-invalid-final-candidate gap.
Theorem 4 is stated as the logically equivalent universal lower guarantee plus a concrete exact-presentation equality witness; a separately named real-valued sInf aggregate is not introduced.
gaps: The source's generalized inverse is not total for bounded deadlines, and Appendix Lemma 4 uses a reversed output-prefix comparison after setting i_j = D^{-1}(t_j); its liminf choice also needs an inverse-range argument or a stricter deadline hypothesis.
Appendix Theorem 12's printed proof ends after the limsup >= 1/2 case split and omits both eventual consistency and the separate <= 1/2 optimality argument.

Algorithm 2's strict-rise queue can retain an early non-target final candidate because Accurate is only eventually subset-valid; Lean uses an explicitly documented queue-all-guesses repair for the constructive theorem.
There is no joint history-dependent randomized-run, filtration, expectation, concentration, or almost-sure convergence interface.
Lemma 1 and Theorems 1--2 lack the adversarial measure-zero-chain construction and Markov/Borel--Cantelli argument.
Lemma 3 and Theorem 3 lack the randomized speculative black-box reduction and Freedman/concentration proof.
No executable implementation, runtime theorem, or human source-correspondence audit is claimed.

claims.title: Impossibility for eventually consistent generators
claims.statement_summary: There is a language family on which every eventually consistent generator has zero timely lower density for every deadline.

source_assessment.notes: The headline claim remains plausible, but the cited Hallucination Barrier route needs repair: the source's bare generalized inverse is undefined for bounded deadlines, and Appendix Lemma 4 uses an invalid output-prefix inequality unless its selected time is an attained deadline value.

formalization.notes: Lean proves the deterministic finite-prefix counting implication used after eventual consistency, but not the universal hard family or almost-sure adversarial argument.

components.summary: Eventual target validity bounds timely credited outputs through an intermediate-language intersection plus a finite burn-in.
Construct one measure-zero-chain family defeating every eventually consistent randomized generator and conclude zero lower density almost surely.

lean_links.notes: This is the deterministic inequality inside the probabilistic impossibility proof, not the theorem's hard-family quantification.

claims.title: Impossibility for linear-time generators
claims.statement_summary: There is a language family on which every generator with vanishing hallucination rate has zero timely lower density under every linear deadline.

source_assessment.notes: The headline claim remains plausible, but its reduction to the Hallucination Barrier inherits the generalized-inverse and reversed-prefix-comparison gap in Appendix Lemma 4. A repaired strict dominating deadline may recover the linear-deadline conclusion, but that repair is not printed or yet formalized.

formalization.notes: The same deterministic pathwise counting inequality is formalized. Its connection to the source's linear-deadline hallucination-rate premise and almost-sure hard-family conclusion is open.

components.summary: Bound finite timely credit by target intersection plus finitely many invalid outputs.
Use the hallucination-rate hypothesis under a linear deadline to obtain the almost-sure zero-density conclusion on the universal hard family.

lean_links.notes: The randomized generator and asymptotic linear-deadline quantifiers are not represented by this endpoint.

relations.notes: Both headline impossibility results are derived from the same Hallucination Barrier construction, though their hypotheses differ.

claims.title: Separation of timely upper and lower density
claims.statement_summary: Under the identity deadline there exists an eventually consistent generator whose worst-case timely upper density equals one half.

source_assessment.notes: Appendix Theorem 12 states eventual consistency and equality mu_up = 1/2, but the printed proof ends after establishing limsup >= 1/2. Its strict-rise queue can also retain an early non-target final candidate. Lean documents this defect, uses a queue-all-guesses repair, and proves the missing consistency and upper-bound arguments with a concrete logarithmic-catch-up adaptive exact presentation.

formalization.notes: A concrete queue-totalized GCG proves stage termination, eventual consistency, cofinal target checkpoints, and the >= 1/2 endpoint for every exact presentation. A finite-history realization drives an adaptive exact presentation whose catch-up exceptions are bounded by Nat.log2 i, yielding <= 1/2 and an unconditional universal-lower-plus-equality-witness characterization.

Prove the finite injective-partner count and the analytic implication from a sublinear catch-up budget to upper timely density at most one half.
Construct an online adaptive exact presentation satisfying the turn-taking certificate and combine its upper bound with the universal lower guarantee.
